Security Guarantees Go Both Ways

Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have asked Russian negotiators to replace Moscow’s 2021 demands with a new European security proposal reflecting today’s circumstances. 

Russia must spell out what it would do to reassure its neighbors, not just the guarantees it wants for itself. Washington asked for “symmetrical steps” to reduce tensions and show that Russia would not attack Europe in the future.

In return, Washington is now willing to discuss issues it previously rejected, including Moscow’s demands on NATO expansion and deployments.

Russia wants the broader agreement negotiated alongside an end to the Ukraine war. European officials in Abu Dhabi agreed to discuss both tracks at once but reserved final decisions on the continent’s security until the war ends. Moscow has resisted European participation in the talks. Washington’s position is that a European security agreement requires European and Ukrainian consent and cannot give Russia a veto over their security choices.

A durable settlement needs both Russia and the governments expected to honor it. The test of Moscow’s new proposal will be what it offers to limit its own power.

Russia and Ukraine have agreed in principle to a major prisoner exchange that Washington says could be the largest of the war. Territory remains unresolved.

After two days of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, both delegations agreed to keep negotiating. The numbers for the exchange have not been finalized. Jared Kushner called territory the hardest open issue and said neither side trusts the other.

Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky insisted that “every inch” of Russian land would be returned, apparently referring to Moscow’s demand for all of Donbas, including territory Ukraine still controls.

Russia also wants a broader European security agreement before the details of ending the war are settled, while European governments want a ceasefire first. Moscow’s delegation refused to meet European representatives in Abu Dhabi, though U.S. envoys say the sides have agreed to include them in the next round.

Until the sides agree on what to negotiate first, the prisoner exchange is the only concrete result.
